1. A thermometer and an electrical heater are inserted into small holes in a solid aluminium block.
[Diagram: cylindrical aluminium block with a thermometer and an electrical heater (leads to power supply) inserted in holes]
The heater is turned on at time $t = 0$. The graph shows the variation of the temperature $\theta$ of the block with time $t$.
[Graph: $\theta$ / °C (15 to 35) against $t$ / min (0 to 6); data points with error bars rising from about 21 °C at 0.5 min and levelling off at about 30 °C]
(a) (i) On the graph, draw the line of best-fit for the data. [1]
(ii) Estimate the initial temperature of the block. [1]
(b) Suggest why the temperature of the block approaches a constant value. [2]
(c) When the temperature has reached a constant value the heater is turned off. The graph shows the variation of the temperature $\theta$ of the block with time $t$.
[Graph: $\theta$ / °C (20 to 32) against $t$ / min (0.0 to 3.0); slightly curved line falling from 30 °C at $t = 0$ to 20 °C at $t = 3.0$ min]
Show that the initial rate of change of the temperature of the block is approximately $-4.0\ \mathrm{K\,min^{-1}}$. [2]
(d) The power of the heater is 52 W. The mass of the block is 0.85 kg. Determine the specific heat capacity of aluminium. [2]
(e) The percentage uncertainty in the rate of change in (c) is 4 %. The percentage uncertainty in the power of the heater is 3 % and that in the mass of the block is 1 %.
(i) Estimate the absolute uncertainty in the specific heat capacity of aluminium. [2]
(ii) Write down the value of the specific heat capacity of aluminium, its uncertainty and its unit. Give your answer to an appropriate number of significant figures. [1]

2.text_clean:
2. The graph shows the variation with time $t$ of the activity $A$ of a sample of protactinium-234.
[Graph: $A$ / Bq (0 to 35) against $t$ / s (0 to 600); points decaying from about 32 Bq at $t = 0$ and levelling off at about 2 Bq]
(a) Suggest why the activity approaches a non-zero constant value. [1]
(b) Estimate the half-life of protactinium-234 explaining your work. [3]

3.text_clean:
3. Two muons are moving parallel to each other with the same velocity relative to the ground.
[Diagram: two muons, one above the other, each with an arrow to the right, above a line labelled ground]
In the frame of reference in which the muons are at rest, the force between them is a repulsive electric force.
(a) Explain, for the frame of reference of the ground,
(i) why there is an additional magnetic force between the muons. [1]
(ii) whether the electric or the magnetic force has the greater magnitude. [2]
(b) In muon decay experiments, muons produced high in the Earth's atmosphere move towards the ground at speeds close to the speed of light. Detectors on the ground record the arrival of muons. Outline how these experiments provide support for time dilation. [3]
3.note: audit: relativity of magnetic force on moving charge; matches equivalents

4.text_clean:
4. The diagram shows two clocks, A and B, that have been synchronized. Clock A is at the origin and clock B is a distance $d$ away in the same inertial reference frame.
[Diagram: clocks A and B on the x-axis separated by distance $d$]
Suggest a way by which the clocks were synchronized. [3]

5.text_clean:
5. A spacecraft leaves Earth with speed $0.800c$, relative to Earth, on its way to a planet that is 12.0 light years away according to Earth measurements.
(a) Calculate the time of arrival of the spacecraft at the planet according to the
(i) Earth. [1]
(ii) spacecraft. [2]
(b) On its way to the planet the spacecraft moves past a cargo ship returning to Earth. The proper length of the cargo ship is 992 m and its speed is $0.600c$ relative to Earth.
[Diagram: spacecraft moving right at $0.800c$; cargo ship moving left at $0.600c$]
(i) State what is meant by proper length. [1]
(ii) Show that the speed of the cargo ship relative to the spacecraft is $0.946c$. [1]
(iii) Calculate the length of the cargo ship according to the spacecraft. [2]
(c) As the spacecraft approaches the cargo ship a light signal is emitted from the front of the cargo ship (F) towards the back (B).
[Diagram: spacecraft moving right at $0.800c$; cargo ship with front F on the left and back B on the right, moving left at $0.600c$]
This situation is represented in the spacetime diagram that shows the rest frame of the cargo ship. F and B represent the front and back of the cargo ship when the light signal is emitted. The scale on the axes is the same.
[Spacetime diagram: grid with $ct$ and $x$ axes; events F and B marked on the $x$-axis, F left of the origin and B right of it]
(i) Construct lines on the spacetime diagram to show the arrival of the light signal at the back of the cargo ship. Label this event using the letter A. [2]
(ii) Determine the time it takes the signal to arrive at the back of the cargo ship according to the spacecraft. [2]

6.text_clean:
6. A proton is accelerated from rest until its momentum becomes $2.50\ \mathrm{GeV\,c^{-1}}$.
Calculate the
(a) potential difference through which the proton was accelerated. [2]
(b) speed of the proton after acceleration. [2]

7.text_clean:
7. (a) Light from a distant bright galaxy arrives at a telescope on Earth after having travelled past a massive galaxy. Multiple images of the bright galaxy are formed.
[Diagram: Earth on the left, massive galaxy in the middle, bright galaxy on the right]
Explain the formation of the multiple images. (You may draw a diagram to help with your answer.) [3]
(b) State what is meant by the event horizon of a black hole. [1]
(c) The radius of the event horizon of a black hole is $R$. A probe is at a distance of $0.25R$ above the event horizon. The probe sends radio pulses at intervals of 1.0 s, according to the probe. Calculate the time between the arrival of the pulses at a spacecraft far from the black hole. [2]

8.text_clean:
8. A net torque acts on a horizontal disk of mass 0.20 kg and radius 0.40 m that is initially at rest. The disk begins to rotate. The graph shows the variation with time $t$ of the angular speed $\omega$ of the disk.
[Graph: $\omega$ / rad s$^{-1}$ (0 to 14) against $t$ / s (0 to 5); straight line from 0 at $t = 0$ to 12.5 at $t = 2$ s, then constant at 12.5]
The moment of inertia of a disk of mass $M$ and radius $R$ about a vertical axis through its centre is $\frac{1}{2}MR^2$.
(a) Show that the angular acceleration of the disk is about $6\ \mathrm{rad\,s^{-2}}$. [1]
(b) Calculate the torque that acts on the disk while it accelerates. [2]
(c) While the disk is rotating at its final constant angular speed, a small object of mass 0.10 kg falls on the disk and sticks to the edge of the disk.
[Diagram: object falling onto the edge of a rotating horizontal disk with a vertical axis]
(i) Calculate the new angular speed of the disk. [3]
(ii) Determine the fraction of the total energy of the disk that was lost. [3]

9.text_clean:
9. A monatomic ideal gas is trapped in a cylinder by a piston. The following data are available.
Initial pressure of gas $= 1.00 \times 10^{5}$ Pa
Initial temperature $= 712$ K
Quantity of gas $= 6.00 \times 10^{-4}$ mol
The gas undergoes an adiabatic expansion to a volume of $8.00 \times 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{m^3}$.
(a) (i) Determine the pressure of the gas after the adiabatic expansion. [3]
(ii) Determine the work done by the gas during the expansion. [3]
(b) The gas then undergoes an isobaric compression until its volume is equal to the initial volume.
(i) Calculate the energy removed in this isobaric compression. [3]
(ii) The gas returns to its original state in an isovolumetric change. The energy supplied during this change is 3.9 J. Calculate the efficiency of this cycle. [1]
(iii) Outline why it is important that engines are designed with high efficiency even though all engines obey the first law of thermodynamics. [1]

10.text_clean:
10. The diagram shows water coming out of a tap (faucet).
[Diagram: tap with a stream of water below it that narrows as it falls]
(a) Water leaves the tap at an initial speed of $1.2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Calculate the speed of the water when it has fallen 0.20 m. [2]
(b) Explain why the diameter of the water stream decreases. [3]
10.note: (a) solvable by kinematics or Bernoulli; tagged X.8 primary plus A.1

11.text_clean:
11. A mass-spring system undergoes damped oscillations with a time period of 5.0 s. At $t = 0$, the system is at maximum displacement. The graph shows the variation of the total energy of the system with time.
[Graph: total energy / J (0 to 12) against time / s (0 to 5); curve decreasing from 10 J at $t = 0$ to 5 J at $t = 5$ s]
(a) (i) Calculate the $Q$ factor for the system. [1]
(ii) Draw, on the axes, a graph to show how the potential energy of the system varies with time. [2]
(b) Explain why engineers must consider resonance when designing structures. [2]

12.text_clean:
12. The diagram shows an object in front of a spherical converging mirror with a focal point F.
[Diagram: upright arrow object on the principal axis to the left of focal point F, concave mirror on the right]
(a) Construct a ray diagram to show the formation of the image. [2]
(b) The mirror is now moved a large distance to the right. Outline the effect of this on the magnification of the image. [2]

13.text_clean:
13. The single-dish radio telescope at Arecibo had a fixed spherical mirror M of diameter of 0.3 km made up of a large number of flat aluminium panels. The antenna was movable.
[Diagram: spherical mirror M set in the ground with an antenna suspended above it by support cables from towers; incoming parallel rays reflected to the antenna]
(a) Explain why a large number of flat panels were used to construct the fixed spherical mirror M. [1]
(b) The telescope was mounted on the ground and could not be steered. Explain how, for one position of the Earth, the radio telescope could gather information from different parts of the sky. [2]
(c) Scientists prefer to mount optical telescopes away from the Earth's surface. Outline two advantages of placing an optical telescope in space. [2]

14.text_clean:
14. A compound optical microscope has an objective lens with a focal length of 10.0 mm and an eyepiece lens with a focal length of 50.0 mm. An object is placed 10.6 mm from the objective lens. The final image is formed at a distance of 250 mm from the eyepiece lens.
(a) (i) Calculate the distance of the intermediate image from the objective lens. [1]
(ii) Calculate the angular magnification of the microscope. [2]
(b) Determine the distance between the two lenses. [2]

15.text_clean:
15. A step-index fibre has core refractive index of 1.47 and a cladding refractive index of 1.45.
(a) (i) Calculate the critical angle at the core-cladding boundary. [1]
(ii) The attenuation of the fibre is $-5.0$ dB. A signal of 12 mW is sent into the fibre. Calculate the output power from the fibre. [2]
(b) Explain, with reference to material dispersion, the advantage of using monochromatic radiation in a fibre. [3]

16.text_clean:
16. (a) (i) Describe how ultrasound is produced. [2]
(ii) Distinguish between an A scan and a B scan in ultrasound medical imaging. [2]
(b) When ultrasound travels from one medium to another the fraction of the incident intensity that is reflected at the boundary is called the reflection coefficient $R$.
The following data are available.
Reflection coefficient at skin–tissue boundary $R_{st} = 7.24 \times 10^{-3}$
Reflection coefficient at tissue–liver boundary $R_{tl} = 5.70 \times 10^{-6}$
A transducer emits ultrasound that is incident on skin. The skin transmits the ultrasound without any loss in intensity. The ultrasound is reflected from the tissue–liver boundary and is received back at the transducer.
[Diagram: transducer against layers of skin, tissue and liver]
(i) Determine the fraction of the emitted intensity of ultrasound that is detected by the transducer. [3]
(ii) In ultrasound scanning the distance of the liver from the skin should not exceed 250 wavelengths. Estimate the minimum frequency needed to scan a liver that is 5.0 cm from the skin–tissue boundary. The speed of sound in tissue is $1500\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. [2]
(c) State one advantage of using ultrasound when studying the internal organs of a patient. [1]

17.text_clean:
17. The parallax angle of the star Vega is 0.131 arc seconds.
(a) (i) Describe what is meant by parallax angle. [1]
(ii) Show that the distance to Vega is 25 light years. [1]
(b) The following information is available for the stars Vega and β Ori.
| | Distance / ly | Luminosity | Temperature / K |
| Vega | 25 | $54 L_\odot$ | 9600 |
| β Ori | 780 | $40\,000 L_\odot$ | 11 000 |
$L_\odot$ is the luminosity of our Sun.
(i) Determine whether Vega or β Ori appears brighter from Earth. [3]
(ii) Calculate the ratio $\frac{\text{radius of } \beta \text{ Ori}}{\text{radius of Vega}}$. [3]
(c) (i) Vega is a main sequence star. Show that the mass of Vega is about three solar masses. [1]
(ii) Discuss whether β Ori is a main sequence star. [2]
(iii) Describe the most likely final stage in the evolution of Vega. [2]

18.text_clean:
18. (a) State what is meant by the cosmic microwave background (CMB) radiation. [2]
(b) The present temperature of the CMB is approximately 2.8 K. Calculate the peak wavelength of the CMB. [1]
(c) The cosmic scale factor $R$ of the universe at the time of the emission of the CMB was 1100 times smaller than its present value.
(i) State what is meant by the cosmic scale factor of the universe. [2]
(ii) Explain how it may be deduced that at the time of the emission of the CMB the temperature of the universe was 1100 times higher than the present temperature. [2]

(i) a star must have a high mass in order to produce heavy elements by nuclear fusion. [2]

20.text_clean:
20. The universe may be considered to be filled with dust of uniform density. A particle of mass $m$ moves with speed $v = H_0 r$ when at a distance $r$ from a point O where $H_0$ is Hubble's constant. Only the mass within a sphere of radius $r$ exerts a force on the particle.
[Diagram: dashed sphere of radius $r$ centred on O; particle $m$ on the surface moving outward with speed $v$]
(a) (i) Show that the point particle will just reach infinity provided that the density is $\frac{3H_0^2}{8\pi G}$. [2]
(ii) Evaluate this density using $H_0 = 68\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$. [1]
(b) In modern cosmology the density in (a)(i) is known as the critical density. Describe the significance of this critical density for models of the universe that include dark energy. [2]
